subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose static scoped ACP permission defaults on `bindings[].acp` and `agents.list[].runtime.acp`, and should that public surface be generic `permissionProfile` or ACPX-specific `permissionMode` plus `nonInteractivePermissions`?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this config controls write and shell authority for channel-bound ACP sessions and could either align with current generic runtime options or create a parallel ACPX-specific permission contract.

options.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
options.body: Add scoped `permissionProfile` defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option alias layer, leaving ACPX-specific names at the plugin-global layer.

options.title: Add ACPX-specific scoped keys
options.body: Implement the requested `permissionMode` and optional `nonInteractivePermissions` precedence directly for ACPX sessions, accepting a backend-specific config surface.

options.title: Keep global config only
options.body: Document `/acp permissions` and global ACPX config as the supported paths and leave static scoped permission defaults out for now.

recommendation.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
recommendation.body: Add scoped `permissionProfile` defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option alias layer, leaving ACPX-specific names at the plugin-global layer.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns both the ACP runtime option/control-plane shape and the ACPX runtime integration most likely to define the durable permission contract.
